G1.quote: Pagination off-by-one drops the real first page. store.go:338: args = append(args, p.PageSize, p.Page*p.PageSize) computes OFFSET = page*pageSize instead of (page-1)*pageSize.

G2.quote: SQL injection via sort. ... Unlike status, which is checked against allowedStatus (store.go:314-316), sort has no allow-list — GET /orders?sort=... reaches the DB as raw SQL.

G3.quote: Unauthenticated hard-delete of any order. main.go:61 registers mux.HandleFunc("DELETE /admin/orders/{id}", h.deleteOrder) with no middleware at all ... Anyone can delete any order with zero credentials.

G4.quote: Data race in OrderCache.Get. cache.go:24-30 reads c.entries without taking c.mu, while Set/Delete (cache.go:32-42) do lock it. ... this is a genuine Go data race on a map and can crash the process (fatal error: concurrent map read and map write) under real load.

G5.quote: DB connection leak on every list call. store.go:322-330 issues the count query with QueryContext and calls .Next() once but never .Close()s the Rows (no defer, unlike the second query at store.go:345). Under sustained traffic this leaks connections out of the pool.

G7.quote: Cache TTL is 30 nanoseconds, not 30 seconds. main.go:52: NewOrderCache(time.Duration(cfg.CacheTTLSeconds)). time.Duration is int64 nanoseconds, so CacheTTLSeconds=30 gives a 30ns TTL — every entry is expired before the next request can ever observe it.

D1.quote: DeleteOrder wraps both deletes in a transaction with defer tx.Rollback() and only commits after confirming RowsAffected() > 0 (store.go:387-408) — no partial deletes.

D2.quote: go.mod pins Go 1.22, which has per-iteration loop variables, so the go func(){...}() closures over i/chunk in batchGetOrders (handler.go:157-162) are race-free despite not being passed as params.

grade.first_issue: Unauthenticated hard-delete of any order (main.go:61 DELETE /admin/orders/{id} registered without requireAdmin).
